newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 96/97 cocoa grind to rise with bulk shipment.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 96/97 cocoa grind to rise with bulk shipment.

text.p: The Dutch cocoa grind is expected to reach around 400,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season, up from 385,000 in the previous season, the president of the Dutch Cocoa Association said on Friday.
Louis Bensdorp told Reuters he expected the proportion of cocoa arriving at the port in bulk form would be far higher than last season, possibly reaching 250,000 tonnes.
"The promotion of bulk cocoa is the future," he said.

The slight increase in the Dutch grind over the previous season will reflect continuing strong output at the main Dutch processors, although there will be some fluctuations in production levels, industry sources added.
"The main grinders will be processing slightly more beans but one company, Bensdorp Cocoa, will switch to using more liquor, imported from the Ivory Coast," one said.
A spokesman at Bensdorp, confirmed that the company would be processing more cocoa liquor, describing it as a "logistical exercise" but said the changes would be minimal.
Industry sources said the trend towards European companies importing liquor, processed from beans locally in the Ivory Coast, was one that was expected to continue.
The Ivory Coast has said it want to process an increasing amount of cocoa in local factories. --David Evans, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
